_comment: RELEASE NOTES. This is the only file to edit when a change should be announced to users.
JSON has no comments, so every key that starts with an underscore is a comment: the loader in core/release_notes.py ignores it. Keep your notes in these keys.
HOW IT IS SHOWN: each signed-in person sees the changes for their own audience in a card at the bottom right of their page, until they close it. Closing is saved for that one account.
RULES (checked by tests/current/test_release_notes_contract.py, so a mistake fails the tests):
1. 'releases' is ordered newest first. Each 'version' is dotted numbers (for example 2.20.26.1) and must go UP for each new release.
The app's current version is the newest release's version. Do not edit it anywhere else.
A change only ever shows to its own audience. A student change never appears on a parent's dashboard, and the reverse.
3. 'text' is the whole message, in plain language for the people who read it. Write it so it makes sense on its own.
4. 'help' is ONLY for 'staff' changes. It must be the slug of a page in the staff guide (see GUIDE_PAGES in blueprints/school/guide.py),
for example 'students' or 'results-report-cards'. Parents and students cannot open the staff guide, so 'family' and 'student' changes must NOT have 'help'.
5. To announce something new, add a release at the top of 'releases' with a new version, a date (YYYY-MM-DD), a title and its changes.
Do not change the wording of a release that people may already have seen; add a new release instead.

releases.title: The portal as an app, the store on the Overview, and Back from the dashboard

changes.text: The portal can now be installed as an app on a phone, tablet or computer, in the school's own name with its logo as the app icon: a bar at the bottom of the screen offers Install (on an iPhone or iPad it says how: Share, then Add to Home Screen), and its x closes it for two weeks. The school's logo is also the icon on every browser tab.

The Overview has a Store panel for the School Admin and anyone with store access: items for sale and in stock, what is running low or sold out, what waits to be collected, this month's sales against last month's, sales per week and the best sellers.
The setup checklist has a new optional step, Open the school store, done once the store has its first item.
Back is never shown on a dashboard, and a dashboard is now where Back starts from: from any page, Back leads at most as far as the Overview.
You can now install the school's portal as an app on your phone: tap Install on the bar at the bottom of the screen (on an iPhone, tap Share, then Add to Home Screen). It carries the school's logo.
You can now install the school's portal as an app on your phone or computer: tap Install on the bar at the bottom of the screen.

releases.title: The school store, faster pages, and a guide with pictures

changes.text: New: the school store. A Store group in the menu has Inventory (items with a price, stock and up to three pictures), Purchase claims (everything bought, until it is handed over) and Record a payment (store payments taken in cash, by transfer or POS). Stock goes down with every sale, from the office or online.
Handing over a store purchase records who collected it, the student or a parent, and texts the parent. A purchase not yet collected can be cancelled, which puts it back in stock.
A new preset role, Store Keeper, runs the store; View the store and Run the store can also be given to any role.

Teaching duties (on a member of staff in Settings, and on Teachers): once you choose a class, the subject list shows only the subjects that class takes. A subject already given to someone stays listed, marked, if the class no longer offers it.
Settings: the Activity log and the notice log (emails and texts sent to parents) are now two tabs side by side, fifty records at a time with Older and Newer, searched across the whole log.
A student's notice log now opens in a pop-up on top of their record, with the same paging and search.
Hiding or showing the setup checklist on the Overview now happens in place, with a spinner, instead of reloading the whole page.
Pages load faster: the browser now keeps the portal's own files, pages are sent compressed, and many pages ask the database far fewer questions. Nothing on them has changed.

The sign-in page gives the school's photographs more room: the school's name, the version and the privacy link now sit on a see-through strip over the photographs, and the school's logo is shown, centred, above Portal Sign In.
The staff guide now has pictures of the screens it describes, and a new page on the school store.

New: the Store, beside Dashboard and Messages. See what the school sells, with pictures and prices, and what you have bought for each child and whether it has been collected. Where the school takes payment online you can buy for any of your children; otherwise pay at the school office.
When something you bought from the school store is collected, you get a text saying who collected it.

releases._comment: Changes since 2.20.26.8: the head teacher / class teacher / subject teacher chain, teaching duties, SSS departments, and Crèche and Nursery classes.
releases.title: Head, class and subject teachers, SSS departments, and Crèche and Nursery

changes.text: The menu has new icons, each drawn for what it opens: a mortarboard for Students, a register for Attendance, an A+ for Academics, a rosette for Report cards, stairs for Promotion, coins for Collections, a price tag for Fee structure and more.

Settings has been redesigned. It opens on what needs attention, then every setting by group with its state; the list of settings stays on the left and each setting opens beside it without leaving Settings, with a search to find one.

Staff (formerly Administrators): adding and managing a member of staff opens in a pop-up with four tabs, and a new password shows in the same pop-up. A role can be opened on top of it to check or change what it allows, without losing what you typed. The Messages tab for writing to colleagues is called Staff too.
Staff roles shows how much each role allows and who holds it. A role opens in a pop-up with its permissions grouped by area and a search, and each holder opens on top of it.
Controls & alerts, the Activity log (searchable, grouped by day, with a Refused-only view) and Online now have been redesigned to match.
When someone without the Entrance examination workspace tries to open one of its pages, they are taken to the school portal and the attempt is recorded in the Activity log as refused.

Teachers and other school staff no longer have the Entrance examination workspace unless the School Admin gives it to them. Without it, signing in goes straight to the school portal; only someone with both workspaces sees Workspace Home and Switch workspace.

Parents has been redesigned: who can be reached by email and text at a glance, each parent's children by name, instant filters and search, and adding or managing a parent (and making them a new password) in a pop-up.
Teachers shows the gaps first: classes with no class teacher and subjects nobody teaches. View it by class or by teacher, and change a teacher's duties in a pop-up.
Subjects can be seen as a list or as a grid of subjects against classes. A new subject, editing one and its locks open in a pop-up.
Attendance has been redesigned: class chips, the school week with the days already taken, one tap per student, Everyone present, live counts, and a term summary that flags anyone under 75%.
Report cards now uses class chips and the new look; the card itself opens in a new tab, ready to print.

Promotion shows its four steps, opens each run in a pop-up where a whole class can be given one decision, and sets class progression in a pop-up that saves as you choose. A committed run can now be read back.
Library has been redesigned: the catalogue and the loans (overdue first, with days late), with adding, editing and lending a book in a pop-up and one-click returns.

Students has been redesigned. It opens on every class at a glance (how many, boys and girls, how many can sign in), and choosing a class or searching loads its register in place. Tick students to archive several at once.

A student now opens in a pop-up with tabs for their profile and portal login, term results, every mark, assignments, projects and school journey. Editing them, their fee account, a new password and corrections open in a second pop-up on top, and saving brings you back to the student.
Registering a student opens in a pop-up, and the login details made for them show there once, ready to print.
Every page that loads in place now shows a spinner while the next view is on its way, inside pop-ups too, and the button you pressed spins until the answer arrives.

New Payments tab in Finance: every payment in one list (all, not yet applied to a fee, fully applied, or voided), by session or method, or found by student, receipt number or payer. It replaces the separate unallocated-payments and allocate pages.

A payment now opens in a pop-up with everything about it in one place: the receipt as issued (print it or open the PDF), Apply to fees with Fill and Fill oldest first, emailing or texting it to the family again, and voiding or refunding it.
Recording a payment, adding a fee item and editing a fee item now open in a pop-up over the page you are on. Record payment finds the student as you type and shows where the receipt will be sent.

A student's account opens in a pop-up from Student accounts. It shows the chosen session's fees with how each is billed (One-time, Full Session, First, Second or Third Term), and that session's payments with the fees each one paid and its receipt.
The menu's groups are now separated by a line, and Finance lists Collections, Payments (with how many are still to apply), Student accounts and Fee structure.

The menu is now grouped the way a school day runs: Overview and Messages at the top, then People (students, parents, teachers), Teaching (classes, subjects, attendance, academics, the exam timetable, report cards, promotion), Finance and Resources. Settings and Switch workspace sit at the foot, beside your name.

Finance is one page with three tabs: Collections, Student accounts and Fee structure, in your school's colours. Collections shows today's and this month's takings, a chart of money in over 7 days, 30 days, 90 days or 12 months against the period before, how it was paid and who took it, and for the session: the share of fees collected, what is overdue, the largest balances, and the same figures by class and by fee.

New Student accounts page: every student's charges, payments, balance, overdue amount and last payment for a session, narrowed by class, by who owes, has part paid, has paid nothing or has paid in full, or by name. Each choice loads in place without reloading the page.

The Fee structure page keeps all its billing steps, pop-ups and the total that stays in view, now in the same look as Academics, with a spinner while a class list, a student's fees or the history loads.

The exam timetable has been redesigned: choose the term with the tabs at the top, see the papers day by day or as a grid of days against classes, and add or edit a paper in a pop-up that can stay open for the next one. Papers that clash, for the same class or in the same room at the same time, are marked and say what they overlap.
Enter offline scores now offers only First Term, Second Term and Third Term; Full Session is no longer a choice.

New assignments, projects, tests, practice tests and examinations are now guided forms that ask one thing at a time, with a step bar showing where you are, and editing an assignment or a project opens in a pop-up over the list. Enter scores is now called Enter offline scores.

Questions for a test, practice test or examination now open in a pop-up over the list. Each question is shown the way students see it, with the right answer marked. You can edit a question where it is, move it up or down and save the new order, add one question after another from the Add a question tab, and change the test's settings, all without leaving the list.
When the setup checklist is hidden, a small bar at the top of the Overview shows how far setup has got, with a Show setup checklist button.

Enter offline scores is redesigned for working down a class: session, term and subject on one line, the class's students on the left with the score each already has, and the Test and Exam side by side with the percentage as you type. Save and next moves straight to the next student without a score, keeping the same maxima. It loads in place and uses your school's own colours.

Results, Assignments, Projects, Tests, Practice tests and Examinations are now one menu item: Academics. Switch between them with the tabs at the top and pick a class from the row of classes below. The lists are compact tables, Results shows a class's students beside the chosen student's term, and everything you open loads in place with a small spinner instead of reloading the whole page.
Report cards for SSS students now show the student's department (Science, Art or Commercial).

The Overview page is now made for you. It shows only what your role needs: the bursar sees today's collections and fees owed, a class teacher sees their class's register, marks to release and report card comments, a subject teacher sees the marks still to send for each subject, the librarian sees loans and overdue books, and the proprietor and head teacher see the whole school. Rankings of students only appear to the teaching staff who need them. It is a compact report: every number is compared with last term, last session, yesterday or last month, and charts show attendance, class and subject averages, the results waiting to be released, collections over time and more.

Staff now follow the school's order: School Admin, then office staff (bursar, admissions, secretary, HR, librarian), then Head Teacher, Class Teacher and Subject Teacher. There are new Head Teacher, Class Teacher and Subject Teacher roles, and the staff form lists roles from the most senior down.

When you register a teacher, a new Teaching duties section sets the class they are class teacher of and the subjects they teach in each class (in SSS, optionally for one department). A teacher then only sees those classes, subjects and students. A teacher can be the class teacher of one class and teach subjects in others; the register, report cards and releasing results stay with each class's own class teacher. Subject teachers set their own tests, practice tests, examinations, assignments, projects and questions for the subjects and classes they teach, and the forms only offer those. The new Teachers page shows every class with its class teacher and subject teachers, and lets a head teacher change who teaches what.

Results now go from the subject teacher to the class teacher. A subject teacher records scores and presses Send to class teacher (for one mark, a student's term, or the whole class). The class teacher releases them to students and parents, or sends a mark back to be corrected. Only the class teacher of a class, a head teacher or the School Admin can release its results.

SSS students now belong to a department (Science, Art or Commercial), set on the student's record, and each subject says which departments take it. Students only see tests for their own subjects, and work issued to a whole class only goes to the students who take the subject.

Crèche and Nursery 1 to 3 classes are now available under Classes (switched off until you activate them). Their pupils work on paper: they do not sign in and get no online tests or assignments. Their teachers record scores under Results, and parents see fees and report cards.
If your child is in Crèche or Nursery, their page in the parent portal now shows just what you need: fees (which you can pay online), released scores and report cards.
If your child is in SSS 1 to 3, their report card now shows their department: Science, Art or Commercial.
SSS students: the tests and examinations you see are now only those for the subjects your department takes, and your report card shows your department.

releases._comment: Changes since 2.20.26.7: one Messages page for colleagues and parents, a Settings page, in-page report cards, and a stricter email setup step.
releases.title: Messages, Settings and a faster report cards page

changes.text: Messages now has two tabs: Administrators and Parents. You can start a conversation with a student's parent yourself (New message), and any administrator who manages parent messages can answer any conversation. Each conversation shows who is currently responding, every reply shows the name of whoever wrote it, and the Open, In progress and Resolved status is kept. Parents' Feedback has moved into Messages.

The menu is shorter: Settings now holds School profile, Academic sessions, Report card settings, Email & SMS, Online payments, Receipts, Administration, Controls & alerts, the Activity log and Online now, grouped and with a search box.

The Report cards page is redesigned. Pick a class, session and term across the top and the students load right on the page with a loading indicator. Beside each student, Comment and Rate traits open a small window, and My signature opens one too. The separate comment and trait pages are gone.

In the setup checklist, Connect email and SMS is no longer ticked off while the school still sends from the platform's shared address. It is now marked as important and is done once the school connects its own email or SMS account.

The parent portal has been redesigned. Your children now sit side by side on the dashboard, each showing fees owing, average and completion at a glance and opening for more. Notifications scroll instead of growing the page, a child's profile is split into Overview, Results, Work and Messages, and the fee account is easier to read and pay from.

The attendance and exam timetable pages are redesigned. Attendance shows the attendance rate, how the days divided, the days to note, and every day laid out by month. The timetable picks out the next paper and lists each day with its papers.

Your attendance and exam timetable pages are redesigned. Attendance shows your attendance rate and the days you were late, absent or excused. The timetable picks out your next paper and lists each day with its papers.
Message the school now looks like a chat: your conversations on the left, the open one on the right, and every message shows the name of the member of staff who wrote it.

Parents now get a text message (SMS, through BulkSMS Nigeria) when a report card is released, a new fee is charged, a payment is recorded, and when the school starts a conversation with them. WhatsApp is no longer used: Email & WhatsApp is now Email & SMS. Whether each school connects its own SMS account or the platform's account is used is set by the platform.
Class teachers now get a notification in their bell two days before a student in their class has a birthday.

You now get a text message for a released report card, a new fee, a payment received, and when the school starts a conversation with you. The school can now message you first. Messages from the school appear under Message school, with the name of the member of staff who wrote each one, and you can reply there.

releases._comment: Changes since 2.20.26.6: Back button, faster fee items and payments, Review assessment, alerts.
releases.title: Back button, faster fees, and fixes

changes.text: Print Login Details on a new or reset student account now prints the student's one-time password along with their username, so you can hand it over on paper.

The setup checklist on the School home page is now complete: it lists the school profile, session, classes, subjects, staff, students, parents, fee items, billing, online payments, receipts, report cards, attendance, timetable, email and WhatsApp, and the library, grouped and with the optional ones marked.
The Back button now returns you to the page you were just on, instead of the workspace chooser or an unrelated page.
Adding a fee item and recording a payment are much faster. The fee structure page no longer loads the whole assessment history up front; it loads when you open that tab.
Review assessment on Bill a student works again and shows a summary before you confirm.
Clicking a notification under Controls & Alerts now shows its full message when it has nowhere else to take you.

releases._comment: Changes since 2.20.26.5: online payments connect again; parents pick which fees to pay.
releases.title: Pay fees online, one at a time or together

changes.text: Online payments now connect to Paystack properly: Test connection checks your keys and tells you if the public and secret keys are from different modes, and parents' payments go through. A payment made for chosen fees is applied to those fees straight away.
Paying school fees online is easier to find and to use. A banner leads you to your child's fees, where you can press Pay beside any one fee, or tick several and pay them together.

releases._comment: Changes since 2.20.26.4: the fee structure buttons use the school's own colours.
releases.title: Fee structure buttons in the school's colours

changes.text: The buttons on the fee structure page use the school's own brand colours, so the page matches the rest of the school's portal. A school that has not chosen colours keeps the standard blue.

releases._comment: Changes since 2.20.26.3: the workspace chooser fits the screen with no scrolling.
releases.title: The workspace chooser fits the screen

changes.text: The workspace chooser (Entrance Examination or School Portal) fits on one screen on desktops, tablets and most phones, so both choices show without scrolling.

releases._comment: Changes since 2.20.26.2: the sign-in page fits the screen with no scrolling.
releases.title: A sign-in page that fits the screen

changes.text: The sign-in page now fits on one screen, so nothing needs scrolling to reach the sign-in button, the help links or the version line. Other password pages are unchanged.
The sign-in page now fits on one screen, so you can see the sign-in button and the help links without scrolling.
The sign-in page now fits on one screen, so you can see the sign-in button and the help links without scrolling.

releases._comment: Changes since 2.20.26.1: work issued to whole classes, the work pages, deletion rules, subjects, the dashboard, the sign-in footer and the guide.
releases.title: Whole-class work, safer deletion and a clearer dashboard

changes.text: Assignments and projects can be issued to a whole class in one step. Choose "Whole class" on the form and every student enrolled in that class receives it. Choose "Selected students" to tick individuals instead.

The assignments and projects pages are redesigned. Pick a class from the grid of tiles, which shows every class and how many items each has. Each assignment or project is a card with its subject, due date, and how many students it reaches.
An assignment or project that has marks, scores or submissions cannot be deleted, because its marks are part of students' term results. It stays on the list.
Deleted assignments and projects can be restored. Choose "Show deleted" on the list to see them, and restore one from its card.

Every subject is listed on the assignment, project, timetable and result forms. A subject not yet offered to the chosen class is marked as such, and it is offered to that class when you save the work.
The Top of the Class card on the dashboard is redesigned around the leader of the term. Only classes with released results are shown.
The dashboard's setup checklist is refreshed from the server about every fifteen minutes, and it is cached in the browser in between.
The What's new panel opens minimised, so it does not cover the page when you arrive. Its cards have a capped height and can be expanded when you want to read them.
The sign-in page shows the platform version at the bottom, read from the release notes.
The staff guide is reorganised into groups that follow the order of a school year, with a new page about the dashboard.
Results & Analytics has a clear gap between its summary cards and the section below.
When a teacher gives an assignment or project to a whole class, every enrolled child receives it, and you are told as before.
Marked assignments and projects cannot be removed once they carry marks, so the marks on your child's report card stay in place.
Assignments and projects given to your class now reach every student in it at once, so nobody is left out of the set work.
Once an assignment or project has been marked, it cannot be removed, so the marks you earned on it stay on your report card.

releases._comment: Newest release first. The date is when the change was made available.
releases.title: Archiving, bulk imports and the staff directory

changes.text: Archive a student, or several at once, from the class register. An archived student leaves the register, the student count and sign-in, and their record stays on file. Restore them from Archived students.
Archived students each have an academic record you can open: class placements, school journey and results by term.
The bulk import page has three steps: students, enrolment history and past results. Each step shows once you pick it, and every import is recorded with who ran it.
Enrolment history rows can record how a student left each year. A graduate is archived once that year is recorded.
Past results can be imported one subject, term and session per row, so a student's record from another system comes across complete.
A new bulk-import permission can be given to any role. It lets that role run all three import steps without holding each step's own permission.
The administrators page is a directory of cards with search and a status filter. Each person's page has a summary, a section list and a save bar.
Looking for a permission under overrides? Search loosely: word order, capitals, accents and small spelling mistakes do not matter.
Past results: once the school has brought in your child's results from earlier sessions, they appear on their academic record and report cards, shown the same way as this year's.
Students who have left the school are archived. Their sign-in is switched off, but they stay on your portal with their records, results and fees.
Past results: once the school has brought in your results from earlier sessions, they appear on your academic record and report cards, shown the same way as this year's.
If you have left the school, your sign-in is switched off. Your records stay with the school.
